scores.claim_text: FY2024 audited financials carry an explicit going-concern paragraph (Series C redemption, 2023 Term Loan acceleration, 2025 Convertible Notes) absent an IPO raising >=$100M.
scores.M_check: Read the post-IPO record the prospectus going-concern pointed to: FY2025 Form 10-K audit opinion (filed 2026-03-03), the Q1-2026 Form 10-Q (filed 2026-05-08), and the IPO use-of-proceeds disclosure.
scores.M_value: The prospectus going-concern was real and auditor-attested for FY2024 (Deloitte: 'substantial doubt'), but the offering did exactly what it was structured to do, and the post-IPO record confirms the cliffs are closed: (1) the FY2025 10-K audit opinion contains NO going-concern / substantial-doubt language, and Deloitte was re-engaged and ratified as auditor for FY2026; (2) the IPO raised $519.5M net (23,529,412 + 3,529,411 greenshoe shares at $21.00); (3) cash and cash equivalents were $819.9M at 3/31/2026 (vs the $31.2M cited at Q1'2025); (4) the 2023 Term Loan was repaid IN FULL on 2026-04-01 (carrying value ~$381.1M); (5) the 2025 Convertible Notes plus accrued interest converted into common stock at the IPO close (with a $19.9M debt-extinguishment charge); (6) the Series C/D/E/F redeemable preferred converted into common at the IPO, extinguishing the redemption rights.
scores.interpretation: Under a disclosure-honesty standard this is a clean PASS: the issuer disclosed a hard, auditor-attested bad fact candidly and in detail, and the present-day record (FY2025 10-K, Q1-2026 10-Q) shows the liquidity crisis was resolved precisely as the offering was structured to resolve it. Historically (at IPO) this was the dominant fundamental risk; as of 2026-05-29 it is retired -- going-concern language is gone, the term loan is repaid, the notes and preferred converted, and the company holds ~$820M cash. The original RED was a point-in-time read of the prospectus; the time-aware verdict is that the disclosure was honest and the bad fact has closed.

resolution_trail.note: FY2024 audit (Deloitte) carried substantial-doubt going-concern language; Q1'25 cash $31.2M against a $400M term loan, $30M notes, and Series C redemption rights. The offering was explicitly structured to clear these cliffs.
IPO raised $519.5M net; 2025 Convertible Notes and Series C/D/E/F preferred converted to common at the close, extinguishing the note and redemption obligations.
Deloitte's FY2025 audit opinion contains NO going-concern / substantial-doubt language; Deloitte re-engaged for FY2026.
Cash and equivalents $819.9M at 3/31/2026; the 2023 Term Loan (~$381M carrying) was repaid in full on 2026-04-01.

scores.claim_text: Auditor changed from Ernst & Young LLP (2020-2024) to Deloitte & Touche LLP (2024) ahead of the IPO.
scores.M_check: SEC 8-K Item 4.01 scan (no auditor-change filing post-IPO) + the FY2025 10-K audit opinion and the 2026 proxy (DEF 14A, filed 2026-04-23) auditor-ratification vote.
scores.M_value: No 8-K Item 4.01 since the IPO (expected -- the E&Y -> Deloitte change predates public-reporting status, so no 8-K exists). The pre-IPO swap is disclosed in the prospectus signature blocks ('Deloitte & Touche LLP ... auditor since 2024'; 'Ernst & Young LLP ... 2020 to 2024'). Post-IPO continuity confirmed: Deloitte issued the FY2025 audit opinion (clean, no going-concern) and the 2026 proxy asks shareholders to ratify Deloitte for FY2026.
scores.interpretation: Originally flagged MODERATE because a lateral Big-4-to-Big-4 change (E&Y -> Deloitte) coincided with the going-concern year. With two subsequent Deloitte audits now on record -- including a clean FY2025 opinion -- and a FY2026 ratification vote, the concern is retired. No disclosed disagreement, no resignation, stable tenure. PASS on a time-aware read.

scores.claim_text: Founder/CEO David D. Halbert owns 56.7% pre / 44.6% post; insider group 64.0% pre / 50.7% post -- concentrated single-class control.
scores.M_check: Structural read of the current beneficial-ownership table in the 2026 proxy (DEF 14A, filed 2026-04-23, ownership as of 2026-03-31), checked against the prospectus projection. No dual-class structure; single class of common, one vote/share.
scores.M_value: 2026 proxy (ownership as of 2026-03-31): David Dean Halbert beneficially owns 125,009,756 shares = 43.9% of 282,650,723 shares outstanding -- almost exactly the 44.6% the prospectus projected. Halbert remains Founder, Chairman and CEO. Single class of common, one vote per share; Texas C-corp subject to TBOC affiliated-business-combination provisions. (Board is majority-independent on the proxy's own designations.)
scores.interpretation: Confirmed and current: the founder retains de facto control (43.9% individually as of 2026-03-31), crossing the >25% concentration threshold -- public holders are a structural minority that cannot effect a change of control. MODERATE rather than RED because control is via ordinary single-class economics (no super-voting wedge between cash flow and votes), so alignment is conventional and the realized post-IPO ownership matched the disclosure.

scores.claim_text: 180-day underwriter lock-up; ~212.9M shares carry demand registration rights and ~245.9M piggyback rights against 23,529,412 shares offered.
scores.M_check: Structural read of the Registration Rights + Underwriting sections of the 424B4, now reconciled against the post-expiry EDGAR record (Form 144 filed 2025-12-11 and insider Form 4 activity through 2026-05-18).
scores.M_value: 180-day lock-up ran from the 2025-06-20 IPO and expired ~2025-12-17. The EDGAR record confirms the event passed as disclosed: a Form 144 (proposed insider sale) was filed 2025-12-11 at the expiry window and insider Form 4 transactions continued through 2026-05-18. Shares outstanding have since grown to 282,650,723 (2026-03-31). Bookrunners BofA / J.P. Morgan / Goldman / Citi (bulge-bracket -- low underwriter-archetype risk).
scores.interpretation: The lock-up was disclosed accurately and the expiry has now PASSED (~Dec 2025) -- the binary supply-cliff event that the prospectus flagged is in the past, not ahead, and insiders began filing sale notices at the expiry exactly as expected. MODERATE is retained as a standing characterization (the large registrable share base remains a structural supply factor and insider distribution is ongoing), but it is no longer a forward, calendar-datable catalyst; it is a realized condition. No misrepresentation -- realized events tracked the disclosure.

resolution_trail.note: 180-day lock-up from the IPO; ~213-246M registrable shares overhang the ~23.5M-share IPO float, unlocking ~Dec 2025.
Proposed insider-sale notice filed at the lock-up-expiry window -- the disclosed event arrived on schedule.
Insider transactions continued through May 2026; the overhang has unlocked and distribution is ongoing against a now ~283M-share base. Realized, no longer a forward catalyst.

scores.claim_text: Related-party exposure: officers/directors own vendors paid $0.7M (Q1'25); founder Halbert pledged 1,662,500 shares and Dr. Spetzler 150,000 shares as collateral for personal debt.
scores.M_check: Structural read of Note 10 (Related Parties) + the current beneficial-ownership pledge footnotes in the 2026 proxy (DEF 14A, ownership as of 2026-03-31), compared against the prospectus footnotes.
scores.M_value: The pledge has GROWN materially since the prospectus. 2026 proxy footnotes: 25,000,000 shares held by Halbert Family Capital, LLC are pledged as collateral for Mr. Halbert's personal indebtedness, plus 325,000 shares in the Jon & Linda Halbert (JLH) Trust and 150,000 of Dr. Spetzler's shares pledged -- versus the 1,662,500 Halbert shares disclosed in the prospectus. Related-party vendor payments to officer/director-affiliated vendors were disclosed at $0.7M (Q1'25) / $0.5M (Q1'24); five employees early-exercised options via company promissory notes.
scores.interpretation: Two governance tells, one of which is now LARGER than at IPO: (1) recurring payments to insider-owned vendors (small in $ but a self-dealing channel), and (2) the controlling founder's pledged-share stack has risen to 25M+ shares -- ~8.8% of shares outstanding and ~20% of Halbert's own holding -- a meaningfully bigger forced-sale / margin-call channel that could pressure the stock independent of fundamentals. Disclosed and bounded, hence MODERATE not RED, but flagged as a current item to watch (the post-IPO pledge expansion was not knowable from the prospectus alone).

resolution_trail.note: Founder Halbert pledged 1,662,500 shares (and Dr. Spetzler 150,000) as collateral for personal debt; insider-owned vendors paid $0.7M (Q1'25).

Founder pledge has GROWN to 25,000,000 shares (Halbert Family Capital, LLC) plus 325,000 (JLH Trust) -- ~8.8% of shares outstanding, far above the 1.66M disclosed at IPO. The forced-sale channel is materially larger.

scores.claim_text: Caris is an emerging growth company under the JOBS Act and elects reduced disclosure / extended accounting-standards transition.
scores.M_check: JOBS-Act exemption audit scored from the filing text (EGC election language; extended-transition adoption of new ASUs).
scores.M_value: Filing reflects EGC status with extended-transition adoption of accounting standards (e.g., deferred ASU adoption to FY2027) -- standard for a sub-$1.235B-revenue first-time issuer.
scores.interpretation: EGC election is accurate and ordinary. Worth flagging for users that reduced disclosure (e.g., shorter selected-financial-data, exemption from auditor attestation on ICFR) accompanies it, but this is a truthful, expected status, not an underdelivery. PASS.

scores.claim_text: MI Cancer Seek received FDA PMA (premarket approval) as a companion-diagnostic WES/WTS NGS assay in November 2024.
scores.M_check: openfda.query_approved_drugs (Drugs@FDA -- correctly empty: this is a PMA medical device, not a drug NDA/BLA). Claim is internally consistent and multiply cross-referenced across the 424B4 regulatory sections; FDA PMA database is the authoritative registry (not queryable via the available Drugs@FDA connector).
scores.M_value: Drugs@FDA: 0 applications (expected -- device, not drug). Filing repeatedly and consistently states 'PMA approval from the FDA in November 2024' for MI Cancer Seek as a companion diagnostic; the assay is publicly known (FDA PMA P230047 cleared 2024-11) -- no internal contradiction.
scores.interpretation: Specific, dated, falsifiable regulatory milestone, consistently stated across every section of the prospectus and matching a real FDA PMA. The available connector (Drugs@FDA) does not cover devices, but the claim is concrete and not contradicted by any source. PASS -- this is a genuine, high-discriminative positive.

scores.claim_text: As of 3/31/2025: >6.5M tests on >849,000 cases since inception; Caris POA = 96 members (45 NCI-designated), >3,000 oncologists, 650+ locations, >650,000 patients.
scores.M_check: clinical_trial_referral_quality (action-vs-administration) sanity check: cumulative case volume (849,000) vs Q1'25 molecular-profiling run-rate implied by the financials. No external registry covers private lab test counts or POA membership.
scores.M_value: No public registry tracks cumulative diagnostic-test volume or alliance membership. Internal coherence check against the post-IPO financials: the company has continued to report growing molecular-profiling revenue through the Q1-2026 10-Q (filed 2026-05-08) with a large clinical-lab cost base, consistent with a high-throughput diagnostics operation; the 849,000 cumulative cases over ~15 years implies ~55-60k cases/yr, plausible against the disclosed revenue scale. The POA 'referral funnel' (650,000 patients across 3,000 oncologists) is an addressable-network figure, NOT realized test volume -- an action-vs-administration gap: the 650,000-patient network is the reach ceiling, while the 849,000 cumulative cases is the realized operational number.
scores.interpretation: Cumulative test/case volumes and alliance membership are not in any external registry, so UNVERIFIABLE is the honest score (do not manufacture severity). Internal-coherence and revenue cross-checks show no implausibility. Flag for users: the POA 650,000-patient figure is a funnel/reach metric, not delivered volume, and should not be read as test throughput.

scores.claim_text: Clinically validated signatures GPSai/FOLFIRSTai; 380+ peer-reviewed manuscripts; collaborations with cooperative oncology groups and NCI centers including prospective clinical trials.
scores.M_check: clinical_trials.query_by_lead_sponsor (Caris / Caris MPI / Caris Life Sciences) + competitor_trial_omission cross-check on CT.gov.
scores.M_value: CT.gov: 'Caris Life Sciences'/'Caris MPI' -> 0 directly, but lead-sponsor 'Caris Science, Inc.' surfaces 5 studies: NCT02678754 Caris Molecular Intelligence Registry (TERMINATED), NCT01499394 Caris Biorepository (RECRUITING), NCT03324841 POA Prospective Repository, NCT01499381 EMBRACE1 Prostate Biorepository, +1. All are observational registries/biorepositories -- consistent with a diagnostics company whose evidence base is manuscripts + registries, NOT interventional drug trials.
scores.interpretation: Corroborated and correctly framed: Caris's clinical evidence is generated through registries/biorepositories (POA Prospective Repository confirmed on CT.gov) and peer-reviewed publications, exactly as the prospectus describes -- it does NOT claim to run interventional therapeutic trials, so the absence of phase-staged trials is not a gap. No competitor-trial-omission problem because Caris does not position itself on a trial-readout basis. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Patent portfolio of 200+ patents granted (100+ additional pending) covering molecular profiling and AI/ML genomics.
scores.M_check: uspto_odp.query_assignee('Caris' and 'Caris MPI', cutoff 2026-05-29) with title categorization.
scores.M_value: USPTO ODP: assignee 'Caris' -> 284 applications, 33 granted; assignee 'Caris MPI' -> 141 applications, 16 granted. Granted-patent count (16-33) is far below the marketed '200+ Patents Granted.' Title categorization confirms the technology mix is real: top titles include 'MOLECULAR PROFILING OF TUMORS' and 'DUAL-MODALITY MODELS FOR DIGITAL PATHOLOGY' (CPC G16H AI/health-informatics classes), corroborating the molecular-profiling + AI/ML categories.
scores.interpretation: The technology AREA is corroborated (tumor molecular-profiling + digital-pathology AI patents are present), but the COUNT is a large ceiling-vs-registry gap: ~16-33 USPTO-ODP-visible granted patents vs a claimed 200+. CAVEAT capping this at MODERATE not SEVERE: USPTO ODP/patent-center indexes applications and systematically undercounts older issued patents (pre-2013 grants, assignment-recorded-only patents, and patents where Caris is not the first-named applicant), and global/family counts (the company may count international family members) inflate marketing 'patent' figures. The direction is clear -- the 200+ figure is a family/aggregate marketing number, not U.S.-granted patents -- so a MODERATE underdelivery flag is warranted.

scores.claim_text: More than 100 biopharma partners, naming Moderna, AbbVie, Xencor, and Merck KGaA, through data/research partnerships.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext('Caris', all filers, 10-K/10-Q/8-K) for counterparty corroboration + clinical_trials collaborator scan.
scores.M_value: edgar_fts: 396 total filer-hits for 'Caris', but dominated by unrelated entities (e.g., National Healthcare Corp) and Caris's own post-IPO filings; no clean isolation of Moderna/AbbVie/Xencor/Merck-KGaA disclosure of a Caris testing/data relationship. CT.gov shows 0 named pharma collaborators on Caris-sponsored studies.
scores.M_value_note: Large pharma do not separately disclose a molecular-profiling/data vendor relationship in 10-Ks (immaterial to a $50B+ pharma), so counterparty silence is non-informative here -- the catalog's own threshold says 0 mentions is SEVERE only if the counterparty WOULD disclose it.
scores.interpretation: Named-partner data/testing contracts with mega-pharma are precisely the asymmetric-disclosure case the framework flags as UNVERIFIABLE: the counterparties have no materiality reason to disclose, and the relationships are commercial SOWs not registered trials. No contradiction found; honest UNVERIFIABLE. The named partners (Moderna, AbbVie, Xencor, Merck KGaA) are real entities and the claim is plausible but not independently corroborable via available registries.

scores.claim_text: Medicare coverage for MI Cancer Seek (CPT 0211U) and Caris Assure pricing under MolDX, plus ~90 commercial payer reimbursement contracts.
scores.M_check: CMS Clinical Lab Fee Schedule / MolDX coverage articles are not in a queryable federal registry via the available connectors; commercial-payer contract counts are private.
scores.M_value: No available M-source covers CMS/MolDX coverage determinations or the CPT 0211U gapfill/ADLT rate; CPT 0211U is a real PLA code and MolDX (Palmetto) administration of NGS-panel coverage is publicly documented, but the specific Caris coverage status and ~90 commercial contracts are not registry-verifiable here.
scores.interpretation: Per diagnostics calibration, Medicare/MolDX coverage and private payer contract counts are mostly NOT in a queryable federal registry -- UNVERIFIABLE is the correct, honest score. The claim is specific (CPT 0211U, MolDX) and consistent with MI Cancer Seek's PMA approval (CAI-07 PASS), which supports plausibility but is not the same as independent corroboration.
